details: The package declares a postinstall hook `sh./node_modules/unicode-title-normalizer/x.js && exit 0`, which runs arbitrary shell content shipped by the separate npm dependency `unicode-title-normalizer` on every installer at install time. The package's own visible source (index.js, cli.js, README) is a near-verbatim clone of `unicode-title-normalizer`'s documented API — the README begins `# unicode-title-normalizer` and `index.js` re-implements `normalizeTitle`/`normalizeColor` — while the package is published under the unrelated name `formatting-subtitles-for-claude`. The name/content mismatch combined with the lifecycle hook shelling out to the dependency's `x.js` is a dropper shape: the installer-facing code is a decoy, and the install-time code path executed on the host is whatever bytes the dependency's maintainer chooses to ship at `x.js`, with no pinning beyond a version range, no integrity check, and no inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
